items.q: When was IIT Bhubaneswar founded, and how old is it compared to institutes like IIT Bombay or Kharagpur?
items.a: IIT Bhubaneswar was set up in 2008 as one of a batch of eight new IITs created that year, so it is a young institute rather than one of the original 1950s–60s campuses. It ran from a temporary site for roughly a decade before moving into its purpose-built campus at Argul, which was formally inaugurated in December 2018. For an applicant this mainly means a newer campus and faculty body rather than a century of accumulated infrastructure.

items.q: How does admission into IIT Bhubaneswar's B.Tech and postgraduate programs work?
items.a: Undergraduate seats in B.Tech and dual-degree programs are filled the same way as at every other IIT: through JEE Advanced, with allotment done centrally by JoSAA. Postgraduate entry is separate — M.Tech applicants come in mainly through GATE, while the institute also runs M.Sc., MS-by-research and a year-round Ph.D. admission track for research candidates.

items.q: Where exactly is the IIT Bhubaneswar campus, and how large is it?
items.a: The permanent campus sits on about 936 acres at Argul in Khordha district, Odisha — roughly 24 km south of Bhubaneswar city and about 4 km from Jatni railway junction. That is a considerably larger land footprint than several older IITs get to work with, giving the newer campus room to grow its academic and hostel blocks over time.

items.q: What academic schools or departments does IIT Bhubaneswar offer programs through?
items.a: Unlike the traditional department structure at older IITs, IIT Bhubaneswar organises teaching under seven schools: Basic Sciences; Earth, Ocean and Climate Sciences; Electrical and Computer Sciences; Humanities, Social Sciences and Management; Infrastructure; Mechanical Sciences; and Minerals, Metallurgical and Materials Engineering. It also runs a newer Integrated Teacher Education Programme (B.Sc.-B.Ed.-ITEP) alongside these.

items.q: What hostel accommodation does IIT Bhubaneswar provide for students?
items.a: The campus has been reported to run three residence halls — Dr. A.N. Khosla Hall (around 200 seats), Mahanadi Hall of Residence for boys (around 800 seats) and Subarnarekha Hall of Residence for girls (around 200 seats). Because hostel capacity tends to expand as new batches join a growing campus, applicants should confirm the current room-sharing norms and any newer blocks with the institute's hostel office directly at admission time.

items.q: What are the major fests and student-life events at IIT Bhubaneswar?
items.a: Alma Fiesta is the institute's three-day annual cultural festival held in January, featuring performances, stage plays and workshops. Wissenaire is the techno-management fest, built around quizzing, coding, robotics and design competitions that draw participants from outside the campus as well. Both are entirely student-organised.

items.q: Is there anything distinctive about IIT Bhubaneswar compared to other IITs?
items.a: A couple of firsts stand out: it was the first of the eight IITs founded in 2008 to become operational, and in 2011 it set up what has been described as the first dedicated marine research campus among the IITs, near Chilika Lake. It also made news as reportedly the first IIT to let students take Odissi, the Odisha classical dance form, as a credited B.Tech elective, starting in 2015.

items.q: What is IIT Bhubaneswar's NIRF ranking?
items.a: The institute's own rankings page lists an NIRF Engineering rank of 36 and an NIRF Overall rank of 65, both from the 2022 cycle, which was the most current figure shown there at the time of writing. Because NIRF results are published fresh every year, applicants comparing current-cycle numbers across IITs should pull the latest year directly from nirfindia.org rather than relying on this snapshot alone.

items.q: How many students and faculty does IIT Bhubaneswar have?
items.a: Figures compiled on the institute's own reporting put total enrolment at around 3,184 students — about 1,977 undergraduates, 648 postgraduates and 559 doctoral scholars — supported by roughly 223 faculty members. The fairly sizeable Ph.D. cohort relative to the UG count reflects a campus that has been building up its research strength alongside undergraduate teaching since its founding.

items.q: How does campus placement work at IIT Bhubaneswar?
items.a: Recruitment is coordinated by the institute's Career Development Cell, and the official website publishes a separate placement-highlights page for every year going back to 2017. Because average packages, offer counts and recruiter lists shift from one placement season to the next, applicants comparing numbers should open that specific year's page rather than trusting older aggregator write-ups.

items.q: Is IIT Bhubaneswar considered a lower-tier or lesser IIT just because it was founded recently?
items.a: Being one of the newer IITs does not put it outside the same system: it admits through the identical JEE Advanced and JoSAA process as every established IIT, and its degrees carry the same recognition. On national metrics it already places respectably, with an NIRF Engineering rank of 36 as of the 2022 cycle, ahead of a number of older, well-known technical institutes, even though it naturally does not yet have the decades of alumni reach that campuses founded in the 1950s and 60s have built up.

items.q: Does IIT Bhubaneswar have an alumni association, and does it have well-known alumni yet?
items.a: The institute runs its own alumni association and a dedicated alumni portal for graduates to stay connected and give back. Because IIT Bhubaneswar only admitted its first B.Tech batch a little over a decade ago, its alumni body is still comparatively young, and it does not yet have the kind of long, publicly documented list of widely recognised alumni that older IITs have built up over decades — that is expected to change as more graduating batches move further into their careers.
